title: Why Are Fire Trucks So Long?
description:
Fire trucks are some of the longest trucks in town. Why so long? Bolt the little tow truck finds out! 🚚
A fun truck fact Short for kids ages 2–6 from Tiny Truck Town.

A fire truck carries long ladders on top. Some ladders can reach as high as a ten-story building! It also carries hoses, and lots and lots of water to spray. Firefighters use it to help keep everyone safe.

title: Excavators Can Spin All the Way Around!
description:
This digger can turn all the way around without moving its wheels. How? Bolt the little tow truck finds out! 🚚
A fun truck fact Short for kids ages 2–6 from Tiny Truck Town.

An excavator's cab sits on a turntable, so it can spin all the way around! Its long arm has a big bucket at the end for digging. And it rolls on tracks, so it won't get stuck in the mud.

title: Why Are School Buses Yellow?
description:
School buses are almost always yellow. Can you guess why? Bolt the little tow truck finds out! 🚚
A fun truck fact Short for kids ages 2–6 from Tiny Truck Town.

Yellow is super easy to see, even far away and on cloudy days. When the bus stops, a little stop sign swings out to tell cars to wait. Then kids can get on and off the bus safely.

title: Why Does the Cement Mixer Keep Spinning?
description:
The cement mixer's big drum spins and spins. Why doesn't it stop? Bolt the little tow truck finds out! 🚚
A fun truck fact Short for kids ages 2–6 from Tiny Truck Town.

Inside is wet concrete. Spinning keeps it mixed, so it doesn't get hard too soon. When it gets to the building spot, the concrete slides out of a chute. Concrete dries hard to make sidewalks and roads.

title: Some Trains Have More Than 100 Cars!
description:
Some trains are so long, you could count cars for a long, long time. How many? Bolt the little tow truck finds out! 🚚
A fun truck fact Short for kids ages 2–6 from Tiny Truck Town.

Some freight trains pull more than one hundred cars! The engine is at the front. It pulls all the cars along the tracks. Train wheels roll on two strong metal rails. Choo choo!
